what_its_for: Carvedilol is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension), heart failure, and to help protect your heart after a heart attack. It belongs to a group of medicines called beta-blockers, which work by slowing your heart rate and relaxing your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard.
how_to_take: Take carvedilol by mouth with food. Eating food with this medicine helps reduce the chance of dizziness or feeling faint. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush or chew it. If you are taking the extended-release capsule (Coreg CR), you may open it and sprinkle the contents on a spoonful of applesauce, but do not chew the beads. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over several weeks. The dose depends on what you are being treated for. A common starting dose for heart failure is 3.125 mg twice a day with meals. For high blood pressure, the starting dose is usually 6.25 mg twice a day. Never change your dose or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first — stopping suddenly can be dangerous for your heart.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store carvedilol at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking carvedilol, as it can increase dizziness and lower your blood pressure too much. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, especially when you first start taking it. Avoid standing up too quickly from a sitting or lying position, as this can cause dizziness or lightheadedness. Do not take over-the-counter cold, flu, or allergy medicines without asking your pharmacist first, as some of these can raise your blood pressure or interact with carvedilol.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: very slow heartbeat (fewer than 60 beats per minute), severe dizziness or fainting, sudden weight gain of more than 2–3 pounds in a day or 5 pounds in a week (a sign of worsening heart failure), shortness of breath, swelling in your legs or ankles, chest pain, signs of low blood sugar if you have diabetes (since carvedilol can mask some of these signs), or any signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of your face or throat, or trouble breathing. Do not stop taking carvedilol suddenly without talking to your doctor.
when_it_works: Carvedilol may start lowering your blood pressure within a few hours of your first dose, but it can take several weeks before you feel the full benefit, especially for heart failure. It is important to keep taking it every day even if you feel well. High blood pressure and heart failure often have no symptoms, so do not stop taking the medicine just because you feel fine.
special_populations: Older adults: You may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering and dizziness effects of carvedilol. Rise slowly from sitting or lying down to avoid falls. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using carvedilol if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it may affect your baby. Breastfeeding: It is not known if carvedilol passes into breast milk. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Diabetes: Carvedilol can hide some warning signs of low blood sugar (like a fast heartbeat). Check your blood sugar regularly and talk to your doctor if you notice any changes. Asthma or breathing problems: Carvedilol should generally be avoided if you have severe asthma or certain breathing conditions. Tell your doctor about all your medical conditions before starting this medicine.
